title: Ươm Hoa
titleFull: Ươm Hoa, a self-watering ceramic pot | Phào Design
description: A two-part ceramic pot that holds water below and draws it up by wick, so the plant thrives without daily watering.
summary: A two-part ceramic pot that holds water below and draws it up by wick, so the plant does well without being watered every day.

heroAlt: The Ươm Hoa ceramic pot in a blue-violet glaze

chapters.heading: The idea
body: Desk plants tend to die for two opposite reasons: nobody waters them, or somebody waters them too much. Ươm Hoa removes the daily watering decision altogether.
The pot splits in two, water below and soil with the plant above. A wick joins the halves and the plant draws up exactly as much as it needs.
points: A channel between the two chambers
The rim flares unevenly to each side
Topped up through the channel, not poured over the soil

chapters.heading: The form
body: The body swells and rounds, while the mouth is cut away into a deep groove and a shallow one, so the shadows shift depending on where you stand.
The glaze is allowed to run, so no two pots come out of the kiln alike.

chapters.heading: Other uses
body: Beyond holding a plant, the same form works as an incense holder, an ashtray and somewhere to stub out a cigarette.
